finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The program is supposed to take a single argument N, which is the size of the matrix. However, if an attacker can control the input, they could potentially inject malicious commands through the argument.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The reported OS Command Injection claim assumes that the untrusted argv[1] value is directly or indirectly used as a format string or argument to a function that constructs an OS command. In this code fragment, argv[1] is only passed to atoi (line 20) to obtain an integer N, which is subsequently used for memory allocation and array indexing. The only printf statements present (lines 16, 53, 54) use either fixed string literals or user-controlled data as ordinary printf arguments, not as format strings. No system(), exec*, popen, or similar command‑execution functions are called, and no shell command is constructed from argv[1]. Therefore there is no path from the untrusted source to an OS command execution sink, so the claim is refuted.
